question.explanation: (D)번에 표시된 'despite'는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 하지만, 바로 뒤의 구문 'it being one of...'는 동명사 'being'의 의미상 주어로 'it'이 쓰여 동명사구를 이끌고 있습니다. 의미상 주어와 동명사가 결합한 구조이므로 전치사인 despite가 이 자리에 오는 것 자체는 문법적으로 올바릅니다. 하지만, despite 뒤에 절(S+V)이 오는 오류로 혼동하기 쉬우며, 이 지문에서 'despite'가 이끄는 부분은 'it being...'이라는 동명사구(명사구)이므로 문법적으로 적절합니다. 아, 질문을 다시 점검해 보겠습니다. 원문 구조: 'despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances'에서 despite는 전치사, 'it'은 동명사 being의 의미상 주어, 'being...'은 동명사구로 통사적으로 명사적 성격을 띠므로 올바른 표현입니다. 그러면 정답(오류)으로 설계한 부분을 확인하겠습니다. 주어 'they(old stained-glass windows)'는 '불어서 형태가 만들어지고(blown)' '단단해진(solidified)' 대상이므로 수동적 의미의 과거분사 'solidified'가 맞습니다. 단, 'solidified'는 자동사로 '어떤 상태로 굳어지다'라는 의미로 쓰여, 수동태 'were blown and solidified'에서 were에 병렬 연결되는 과거분사 형태입니다. 이를 'solidifying'으로 바꾸어 수동 관계 및 병렬 구조(were blown and solidified)를 깨뜨린 형식을 취했습니다. 따라서 (D) 'solidifying'은 'solidified'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect as it might __(A) appear__ to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, __(B) thicker__ at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass __(C) is__ slowly sinking over time. Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and __(D) solidifying__ in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is that, __(E) despite__ it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.

By lowering the cost of data collection, mining, and analysis in drug development and clinical trials, AI can help offset imbalances in the pharmaceutical industry that direct attention to diseases that "pay," whether because the disease is more common or because it is prevalent among demographics that can __(E) to pay__ more. We see the democratizing power of AI to broaden the attention of the medical and research communities to find cures to traditionally neglected health issues and among traditionally neglected populations.

question.passageWithMarkers: In the pharmaceutical industry, algorithms are __(A) being employed__ to find treatments and drugs for rare diseases that to date haven't received much attention. The hard truth has always been __(B) that__ pharma devotes more research and development resources to diseases that affect the rich. The definition of rare has too often __(C) been associated__ with poor ― that is, even if a disease is quite prevalent in a population that cannot afford to pay for it (for example, people __(D) lives__ in the developing world), the disease has been neglected compared to First World illnesses. By lowering the cost of data collection, mining, and analysis in drug development and clinical trials, AI can help offset imbalances in the pharmaceutical industry that direct attention to diseases that "pay," whether because the disease is more common or because __(E) it__ is prevalent among demographics that can pay more. We see the democratizing power of AI to broaden the attention of the medical and research communities to find cures to traditionally neglected health issues and among traditionally neglected populations.

question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect as __(A) it__ might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an __(B) imperceptibly__ viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, __(C) is__ generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time. Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they __(D) were blown__ and solidified in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest __(E) human-made__ substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.

minorIssues: The explanation of (B) states it refers to 'the technical term for this mess', but it actually refers exophorically or structurally to 'this mess' itself or serves as a dummy pronoun. It does not affect the grammatical correctness of 'it' though.
strengths: The target (C) features a classic long-distance subject-verb agreement trap with multiple distractor/inserted clauses (sheets ... is).
Option (E) 'despite it being' beautifully tests the gerund with its subject, which is highly elegant and genuinely CSAT-grade.
llmJudge.improvementHint: The distractor (E) despite it being is great, but make sure to emphasize in the future that 'it' acts as the accusative/possessive subject of the gerund being.

question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is __(A) slowly__ sinking over time. Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances __(B) are__ they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is __(C) that__, despite it __(D) to be__ one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; __(E) it__'s a state.

question.passageWithMarkers: In the pharmaceutical industry, algorithms are __(A) being employed__ to find treatments and drugs for rare diseases __(B) that__ to date haven't received much attention. The hard truth has always been that pharma devotes more research and development resources to diseases that affect the rich. The definition of rare has too often __(C) been associating__ with poor ― that is, even if a disease is quite prevalent in a population that cannot afford to pay for __(D) it__ (for example, people __(E) living__ in the developing world), the disease has been neglected compared to First World illnesses. By lowering the cost of data collection, mining, and analysis in drug development and clinical trials, AI can help offset imbalances in the pharmaceutical industry that direct attention to diseases that "pay," whether because the disease is more common or because it is prevalent among demographics that can pay more. We see the democratizing power of AI to broaden the attention of the medical and research communities to find cures to traditionally neglected health issues and among traditionally neglected populations.

majorIssues: The target error in (E) occurs twice in the passage text, but only the second one is marked as neglecting. This inconsistency slightly hurts clarity.

minorIssues: Explanations for incorrect options are very standard, missing deeper linguistic nuances or trick elements present in premium items.
strengths: The passage is highly intellectual, topical, and aligns perfectly with CSAT-style topics on technology and ethics.
The explanations and Korean translations are linguistically sound and free of terminological errors.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
question.explanation: (E)의 neglecting은 어법상 틀렸다. 'traditionally neglected health issues and ... populations'에서 보건 문제와 인구집단은 스스로 무시하는 행위의 주체가 아니라 오히려 무시당하는 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 neglected가 명사를 수식해야 한다. 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 neglecting을 쓰면 '스스로 무시하는 문제/인구'라는 어색하고 부적절한 의미가 되어 문맥상 맞지 않다. 따라서 neglecting은 neglected로 고쳐야 한다.
